title: The Ship of Theseus: What Makes Something Truly the Same?
speaker: Tom Wilkinson

keywords.def: A thought experiment helps philosophers imagine what would happen if one part of a situation changes.
Your identity includes your name, personality, and the things that make you different from others.
Mythology tells us stories about gods, heroes, and ancient events that explain a culture’s beliefs.
A paradox is a problem or statement that seems impossible but makes you think deeply.
Continuity means something stays connected or the same over time without interruption.
The function of a tool or machine is what it is used for or what it does.

sentences.en: What makes something the same object over time, even if all of its parts are replaced?
sentences.zh: 即使所有的部件都被更换了，是什么让某样东西随着时间的推移依然是同一个物体？

sentences.en: This might sound like a strange question, but it’s one of the oldest and most interesting puzzles in philosophy.
sentences.zh: 这听起来可能是一个奇怪的问题，但它是哲学中最古老、最有趣的谜题之一。

sentences.en: And we still ask similar questions all the time: about identity, technology, artificial intelligence, and ourselves.
sentences.zh: 而且我们现在也一直在问类似的问题：关于认同、技术、人工智能以及我们自己。

sentences.en: If you change over time, your personality, your body, your memories… are you still the same you?
sentences.zh: 如果你随着时间而改变，你的性格、你的身体、你的记忆……你还是原来的你吗？

sentences.en: In today’s episode of Thinking in English, we’re going to explore this fascinating idea through one of history’s most famous thought experiments: the Ship of Theseus.
sentences.zh: 在今天这期《Thinking in English》节目中，我们将通过历史上最著名的思想实验之一：忒修斯之船，来探讨这个迷人的观点。

sentences.en: As always, this episode is designed to help you improve your English.
sentences.zh: 和往常一样，本期节目的旨在帮助你提高英语水平。

sentences.en: I’ll introduce you to useful vocabulary, explain ideas clearly, and make you think more deeply in English.
sentences.zh: 我将向你介绍有用的词汇，清晰地解释观点，并让你用英语进行更深层次的思考。

sentences.en: Let me start with a real life example. A few years ago I was watching a video on YouTube about watch repair.
sentences.zh: 让我从一个现实生活中的例子开始。几年前，我在YouTube上观看了一个关于手表修理的视频。

sentences.en: I’ve been fascinated by Wristwatches for a few years.
sentences.zh: 几年来，我一直对手表很着迷。

sentences.en: I like to learn about how they work, how they’re built, and how skilled watchmakers can take something old and broken and make it work like new again.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢了解它们的工作原理、建造方式，以及熟练的钟表匠如何将旧的、坏的东西变得像新的一样运转。

sentences.en: In the video, the watchmaker was restoring a beautiful vintage watch, but some parts of the watch were completely broken or too damaged to fix.
sentences.zh: 在视频中，这位钟表匠正在修复一块精美的古董表，但手表的某些部分已经完全损坏或受损太严重而无法修复。

sentences.en: So he replaced them. He added a new glass cover, new hands, a new strap, new springs and screws inside the movement, which is the parts that makes the watch work.
sentences.zh: 所以他更换了它们。他加了一个新的玻璃镜面、新的指针、新的表带、机芯内部的新弹簧和螺丝，机芯就是让手表运转的部件。

sentences.en: By the end of the repair the watch looked amazing.
sentences.zh: 修理结束时，这块手表看起来棒极了。

sentences.en: It worked perfectly. But many of its parts, maybe 25 to 50% were completely new.
sentences.zh: 它运转完美。但它的许多部件，也许25%到50%已经是全新的了。

sentences.en: That made me wonder, is it still the same watch?
sentences.zh: 这让我怀疑，它还是原来的那块表吗？

sentences.en: This leads us to an ancient question that philosophers have been debating for over 2000 years.
sentences.zh: 这引导我们走向一个哲学家们已经争论了2000多年的古老问题。

sentences.en: And it all goes back to a hero from Greek mythology: Theseus.​ The myth of Theseus is a famous story that I’m sure many of you have heard before.
sentences.zh: 这一切都可以追溯到希腊神话中的英雄：忒修斯。忒修斯的神话是一个著名的故事，我相信你们很多人以前都听说过。

sentences.en: Theseus was a prince of Athens, but as a child he didn’t know he was royalty.
sentences.zh: 忒修斯是雅典的王子，但小时候他并不知道自己是皇室成员。

sentences.en: He grew up far away from the city with his mother.
sentences.zh: 他和母亲一起在远离城市的地方长大。

sentences.en: When he became a young man, he discovered the truth.
sentences.zh: 当他成为一个年轻人的时候，他发现了真相。

sentences.en: That he was the son of the king and the rightful heir to the throne of Athens.
sentences.zh: 他是国王的儿子，也是雅典王位的合法继承人。

sentences.en: At that time, Athens had a terrible problem.
sentences.zh: 当时，雅典有一个可怕的问题。

sentences.en: Every year, the city had to send seven boys and seven girls to the island of Crete.
sentences.zh: 每年，这座城市都必须向克里特岛送去七个男孩和七个女孩。

sentences.en: Why? Because of a cruel agreement with King Minos of Crete.
sentences.zh: 为什么？因为与克里特岛米诺斯国王的一个残酷协议。

sentences.en: These young people were sent into a dark and dangerous labyrinth.
sentences.zh: 这些年轻人被送进了一个黑暗而危险的迷宫里。

sentences.en: A huge maze built under the city. Inside the maze lived a terrifying monster.
sentences.zh: 一个建在城市下面的巨大迷宫。迷宫里住着一个可怕的怪物。

sentences.en: The Minotaur. The Minotaur was a creature that was half man and half bull.
sentences.zh: 米诺陶洛斯。米诺陶洛斯是一个半人半牛的生物。

sentences.en: The Minotaur would eat the children and no one had ever escaped.
sentences.zh: 米诺陶洛斯会吃掉这些孩子，而且从来没有人逃脱过。

sentences.en: Theseus wanted to prove that he was brave and worthy of being king.
sentences.zh: 忒修斯想证明自己是勇敢的，并且配得上做国王。

sentences.en: So he volunteered to go to Crete and face the Minotaur.
sentences.zh: 所以他自愿去克里特岛面对米诺陶洛斯。

sentences.en: Before he left, his father gave him two sets of sails, white sails and black sails.
sentences.zh: 在他离开之前，他的父亲给了他两套帆，白帆和黑帆。

sentences.en: Sails are the part of the ship that catches the wind.
sentences.zh: 帆是船上捕捉风的部分。

sentences.en: Theseus promised to return with white sails if he survived, and black sails if he died or failed.
sentences.zh: 忒修斯承诺如果他生还就会挂白帆回来，如果他死了或失败了就会挂黑帆。

sentences.en: Theseus and the other young Athenians boarded a ship and sailed to Crete.
sentences.zh: 忒修斯和其他年轻的雅典人登上一艘船，驶向克里特岛。

sentences.en: The ship they used is the famous Ship of Theseus In Crete, something unexpected happened.
sentences.zh: 他们使用的船就是著名的忒修斯之船。在克里特岛，发生了意想不到的事情。

sentences.en: Theseus, met a princess, the daughter of King Minos.
sentences.zh: 忒修斯遇到了一位公主，米诺斯国王的女儿。

sentences.en: She fell in love with Theseus and wanted to help him.
sentences.zh: 她爱上了忒修斯并想帮助他。

sentences.en: Secretly, she gave him a ball of thread and a sword.
sentences.zh: 她秘密地给了他一团线和一把剑。

sentences.en: Theseus used the sword to fight and kill the Minotaur, and he used the thread to find his way back out of the labyrinth.
sentences.zh: 忒修斯用剑与米诺陶洛斯战斗并杀死了它，他又用线找到了走出迷宫的路。

sentences.en: He saved the other children, escaped Crete and sailed back to Athens.
sentences.zh: 他救了其他孩子，逃离了克里特岛并乘船返回雅典。

sentences.en: But on the way home, Theseus made a tragic mistake.
sentences.zh: 但在回家的路上，忒修斯犯了一个悲惨的错误。

sentences.en: He forgot to change the sails. He arrived in Athens with black sails flying from the ship.
sentences.zh: 他忘记换帆了。他抵达雅典时，船上挂着黑帆。

sentences.en: His father, the King, saw the black sails and believed his son had died.
sentences.zh: 他的父亲，也就是国王，看到黑帆后相信他的儿子已经死了。

sentences.en: In his grief, the king jumped off a cliff into the sea.
sentences.zh: 在悲痛中，国王跳崖殉海。

sentences.en: Theseus became the new king of Athens. To honor his journey and his father’s death, the people of Athens kept the ship as a symbol of courage and heroism.
sentences.zh: 忒修斯成为了雅典的新国王。为了纪念他的旅程和父亲的死，雅典人民将这艘船作为勇气和英雄主义的象征保留了下来。

sentences.en: They repaired it and protected it for many generations.
sentences.zh: 他们世世代代修理它并保护它。

sentences.en: This legendary ship, the Ship of Theseus, is now at the center of a fascinating thought experiment.
sentences.zh: 这艘传奇的船，忒修斯之船，现在正处于一个迷人的思想实验的核心。

sentences.en: What happens to something when you keep repairing it, replacing its parts, and changing it over time?
sentences.zh: 当你不断修理它、更换它的零件并随着时间改变它时，会发生什么？

sentences.en: Is it still the same? ​ The earliest version of this thought experiment that I could find comes from the Greek writer and philosopher, Plutarch.
sentences.zh: 它还是原来的样子吗？我能找到的最早的这个思想实验的版本来自希腊作家和哲学家普鲁塔克。

sentences.en: In his book, the Life of Theseus, Plutarch described how the people of Athens took care of Theseus’s ship.
sentences.zh: 在他的书《忒修斯传》中，普鲁塔克描述了雅典人民是如何照顾忒修斯的船的。

sentences.en: As the wooden planks began to rot or break, they replaced them one by one.
sentences.zh: 随着木板开始腐烂或破裂，他们一块一块地更换它们。

sentences.en: First a board here, and then a beam there.
sentences.zh: 先是这里的一块板，然后是那里的根梁。

sentences.en: Slowly, piece by piece, the ship was repaired.
sentences.zh: 慢慢地，一块接一块，这艘船得到了修复。

sentences.en: Eventually, every single part of the ship had been replaced.
sentences.zh: 最终，船上的每一个零件都被更换了。

sentences.en: None of the original wood remained. And this created a puzzle or a paradox.
sentences.zh: 原来的木头一点也没有剩下。这就产生了一个谜题或悖论。

sentences.en: Plutarch wrote; “The ship wherein Theseus and the youth of Athens returned from Crete, had 30 oars, and was preserved by the Athenians.
sentences.zh: 普鲁塔克写道：“忒修斯和雅典青年从克里特岛返回的那艘船有30支桨，被雅典人保存了下来。

sentences.en: For they took away the old planks as they decayed, putting in new and stronger timber in their places.
sentences.zh: 因为他们随着旧木板的腐烂而把它们拿走，在它们的位置上换上更新更结实的木材。

sentences.en: The ship became a standing example among the philosophers for the logical question of things that grow.
sentences.zh: 这艘船成了哲学家们关于事物生长逻辑问题的一个常备例子。

sentences.en: One side holding that the ship remained the same and the other contending that it was not the same.”
sentences.zh: 一方认为这艘船保持不变，另一方则争辩说它已经不是同一艘船了。”

sentences.en: So here’s the basic question. Is this still the same ship of Theseus?
sentences.zh: 所以，基本问题来了。这还是原来的忒修斯之船吗？

sentences.en: If none of the original parts are left, can we still call it his ship?
sentences.zh: 如果原来的零件一个都不剩了，我们还能叫它他的船吗？

sentences.en: Or has it become something completely new?
sentences.zh: 还是它已经变成了全新的东西？

sentences.en: This is not just about ships. The same question can be asked about anything, like the watch I mentioned earlier.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅关于船。对于任何事情都可以问同样的问题，就像我前面提到的手表一样。

sentences.en: If all of the parts are changed, is it still the same object?
sentences.zh: 如果所有的零件都换了，它还是同一个物体吗？

sentences.en: We can also ask this about ourselves. You are not made of the same cells you had as a child.
sentences.zh: 我们也可以对我们自己提出这个问题。你身上的细胞已经不是你小时候的那些了。

sentences.en: Scientists say the human body replaces most of its cells every seven to 10 years.
sentences.zh: 科学家说，人体每七到十年就会更换大部分细胞。

sentences.en: Your thoughts, your memories, even your personality change over time.
sentences.zh: 你的思想、你的记忆，甚至你的性格都会随着时间而改变。

sentences.en: So are you still the same person you were 10 years ago?
sentences.zh: 所以你还是10年前那个你吗？

sentences.en: More than a thousand years after Plutarch, the English philosopher Thomas Hobbes added an extra layer to the ship of Theseus puzzle.He made the question even harder to answer.
sentences.zh: 在普鲁塔克之后一千多年，英国哲学家托马斯·霍布斯为忒修斯之船的谜题增加了一个额外的层面。他让这个问题更难回答了。

sentences.en: Remember how the Athenians repaired the ship by replacing the old wooden parts with new ones.
sentences.zh: 还记得雅典人是如何通过用新木质零件替换旧木质零件来修理这艘船的吗？

sentences.en: Hobbes asked, What if someone didn’t throw away the old parts?
sentences.zh: 霍布斯问，如果有人没有扔掉旧零件会怎么样？

sentences.en: What if they saved every plank, nail and oar that had been removed?
sentences.zh: 如果他们保存了每一个被拆下来的木板、钉子和船桨呢？

sentences.en: Then imagine this. Someone takes those original parts, carefully repairs them and uses them to build a second ship.
sentences.zh: 然后想象一下。有人拿走了那些原有的零件，仔细修理它们，并用它们建造了第二艘船。

sentences.en: A ship made completely from the old original materials.
sentences.zh: 一艘完全由旧的原始材料制成的船。

sentences.en: Now there are two ships. The first ship in Athens has been repaired and maintained over time.
sentences.zh: 现在有两艘船了。雅典的第一艘船随着时间的推移得到了修理和维护。

sentences.en: It looks just like the original, but it’s made from completely new parts.
sentences.zh: 它看起来就像原版一样，但它完全由新零件制成。

sentences.en: The second ship has been rebuilt using the actual old parts, the ones Theseus really touched and used during his journey.
sentences.zh: 第二艘船是用实际的旧零件重建的，也就是忒修斯在旅途中真正触摸和使用过的零件。

sentences.en: Which one is the real ship of Theseus? Is it the ship that has stayed in Athens, always being repaired and used, but with new parts?
sentences.zh: 哪一个是真正的忒修斯之船？是那艘一直留在雅典、不断被修理和使用但带有新零件的船吗？

sentences.en: Or is it the one that has been rebuilt from the original historical materials, even if it hasn’t been used for years?
sentences.zh: 还是那艘用最初的历史材料重建的船，尽管它已经很多年没用了？

sentences.en: Some people say the repaired ship is the real one because it has continuity.
sentences.zh: 有些人说修好的船是真的，因为它具有连续性。

sentences.en: It has a history of use and a connection to the city.
sentences.zh: 它有着使用的历史和与这座城市的联系。

sentences.en: Others say the reconstructed ship is the true original because it contains the real materials Theseus once used.​ I think the ship of Theseus thought experiment is actually a powerful way to think about modern life technology and who we are as people.
sentences.zh: 其他人则说重建的船才是真正的原版，因为它包含忒修斯曾经用过的真实材料。我认为忒修斯之船的思想实验实际上是思考现代生活技术以及我们作为人的身份的一种有力方式。

sentences.en: Think about a smartphone. Over time, you might replace the screen as it cracks, upgrade the battery, add a new case, or even change the internal parts.
sentences.zh: 想想智能手机。随着时间的推移，你可能会在屏幕破裂时更换它、升级电池、添加新外壳，甚至更换内部零件。

sentences.en: At what point does it stop being your original phone?
sentences.zh: 在哪个时间点它就不再是你的原装手机了？

sentences.en: Is it still your phone if none of the original parts are left?
sentences.zh: 如果原来的零件一个都不剩了，它还是你的手机吗？

sentences.en: Or what about a classic car? Some people restore old cars by replacing almost every part.
sentences.zh: 或者经典汽车呢？有些人通过更换几乎所有零件来修复老式汽车。

sentences.en: New engines, new wheels, new paint, but they still call it the same car… is it?
sentences.zh: 新引擎、新车轮、新油漆，但他们仍然叫它同一辆车……是这样吗？

sentences.en: Imagine a robot that slowly upgrades over time.
sentences.zh: 想象一个随着时间慢慢升级的机器人。

sentences.en: It gets new arms, new processors, and even a new memory system.
sentences.zh: 它得到了新手臂、新处理器，甚至是新的记忆系统。

sentences.en: If it’s constantly changing and updating, is it still the same robot?
sentences.zh: 如果它在不断变化和更新，它还是同一个机器人吗？

sentences.en: Let’s go even further. Think about culture.
sentences.zh: 让我们走得更远。想想文化。

sentences.en: A country or a city changes its buildings, its language, and its traditions over time, but we still call it the same place.
sentences.zh: 一个国家或城市随着时间的推移改变了它的建筑、语言和传统，但我们仍然称它为同一个地方。

sentences.en: Japan today is very different from Japan 1000 years ago.
sentences.zh: 今天的日本与1000年前的日本非常不同。

sentences.en: So why do we still call it Japan? France today is completely different to the France from 1000 years ago.
sentences.zh: 那为什么我们还叫它日本？今天的法国与1000年前的法国完全不同。

sentences.en: Britain today is completely different from the Britain 1000 years ago.
sentences.zh: 今天的英国与1000年前的英国完全不同。

sentences.en: Are these still the same countries? Are these still the same places?
sentences.zh: 这些还是同一个国家吗？这些还是同一个地方吗？

sentences.en: Or imagine a company that gets new employees, new owners, and even a new name.
sentences.zh: 或者想象一家拥有新员工、新老板甚至新名称的公司。

sentences.en: Is it still the same business? The ship of Theseus helps us explore all of these situations.
sentences.zh: 它还是同一家企业吗？忒修斯之船帮助我们探索所有这些情况。

sentences.en: It makes us ask: What makes something the same over time?
sentences.zh: 它让我们发问：是什么让某样东西随着时间的推移保持不变？

sentences.en: Is it the parts, the function, the name, the memories? ​ Philosophers have tried to solve the Ship of Theseus problem.
sentences.zh: 是零件、功能、名字、还是记忆？哲学家们曾试图解决忒修斯之船的问题。

sentences.en: First, there’s the ancient philosopher, Heraclitus.
sentences.zh: 首先，是古代哲学家赫拉克利特。

sentences.en: He tried to solve the issue by thinking about water.He wrote, You can never step into the same river twice.
sentences.zh: 他试图通过思考水来解决这个问题。他写道，人不能两次踏入同一条河流。

sentences.en: He meant that a river is always changing.
sentences.zh: 他的意思是河流总是在变化的。

sentences.en: The water flows and is never exactly the same from one moment to the next.
sentences.zh: 水在流动，从一个时刻到下一个时刻绝不完全相同。

sentences.en: Yet we still call it the same river. He thought that change is natural.
sentences.zh: 然而我们仍然称它为同一条河。他认为改变是自然的。

sentences.en: Things stay the same, only because we give them a name and a meaning.
sentences.zh: 事物保持不变，只是因为我们赋予了它们名称和意义。

sentences.en: Other thinkers say what matters is continuity over time.It’s not the material parts that make something the same, but the continuous existence or function.
sentences.zh: 其他思想家则认为，重要的是随时间推移的连续性。使某物保持不变的不是物质部分，而是连续的生存或功能。

sentences.en: For example, a car that is repaired and maintained over many years is still the same car because it has a continuous use and history.
sentences.zh: 例如，一辆经过多年修理和维护的汽车仍然是同一辆汽车，因为它具有连续的使用和历史。

sentences.en: The same idea applies to people. We are the same person because our mind and memories continue even if our bodies change.
sentences.zh: 同样的道理也适用于人。我们是同一个人，因为我们的思想和记忆在继续，即使我们的身体发生了变化。

sentences.en: However, there is no single answer that everyone agrees on.​
sentences.zh: 然而，并没有一个所有人都能达成一致的答案。

sentences.en: Now it’s time for your thoughts. What do you think?
sentences.zh: 现在是你想想的时候了。你怎么看？

sentences.en: Is something still the same if all its parts are replaced?
sentences.zh: 如果所有零件都被更换了，某样东西还是原来的东西吗？

sentences.en: Or does it become something new? Which ship would you choose as the real Ship of Theseus: the repaired one or the one rebuilt from the original parts?
sentences.zh: 还是它变成了新的东西？你会选择哪艘船作为真正的忒修斯之船：修好的那艘，还是用原零件重建的那艘？

sentences.en: And what about yourself? Are you the same person you were ten years ago?
sentences.zh: 那你自己呢？你还是十年前的那个你吗？

sentences.en: Why or why not? Thinking about these questions in English is a great way to practice your language skills and to improve your ability to discuss complex ideas!
sentences.zh: 为什么是或者为什么不是？用英语思考这些问题是练习语言技能和提高讨论复杂想法能力的绝佳方式！

sentences.en: Leave a comment with your opinion on the Ship of Theseus!
sentences.zh: 留下评论，分享你对忒修斯之船的看法！
